newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state sells part of stake via GDRs.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state sells part of stake via GDRs.

text.p: The Egyptian state on Wednesday sold 20 percent of its stake in private sector Misr International Bank/MIBANK to investors via global depository receipts (GDRs), the sale agents said.

The agent, who declined to be named, told Reuters the GDR offering of 800,000 shares had been more than seven times oversubscribed. London-based securities house Nomura International were the lead managers of the deal.
The GDRs were sold for $15.80 each and will be listed on London's SEAQ International market, the agent said. Ten GDRS are equivalent to one MIBANK share.
The agent said the GDR price was at a 3.1 percent discount to MIBANK's 552.16 pound closing price on the Egyptian stock exchange on Tuesday. On Wednesday, the stock closed at 535 pounds ($15.78).

"We had about $800 million of demand. British investors have taken up 30 percent of the deal, U.S. investors 25 percent while Asian investors took 10 percent. The rest was covered by European and Middle Eastern investors," the agent said.
"This is the first Egyptian GDR with any placement in the Asian region," he added.

The MIBANK offering is the second GDR for an Egyptian bank and the country's fourth. Commercial International Bank GDRs are already trading in London as are Suez Cement and privatised al-Ahram Beverages, also known Pyramids Beverages.

After the GDR, the government-owned Banque Misr's stake in MIBANK shrinks to 24.4 percent from 44.4 percent, although state-owned Misr Insurance still holds 4 percent. The stake of private investors has risen to 44.6 percent of the bank.
Other shareholders are Banca di Roma International, The British Arab Commercial Bank Ltd, Europartners Holding and Sakura Bank Ltd.
